newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currency futures end volatile trade lower.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currency futures end volatile trade lower.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures ended a session of relatively thin, often volatile trading lower.

Although futures cut losses during the final hour when some fund selling subsided, March marks, Swiss francs and yen still finished with hefty losses after each sagged to new a contract low near midday Friday.
Nearby yen fell to $0.008648, marks skidded to $0.6403 and Swiss francs dropped to as low as $0.7386 as U.S. Treasury bonds and equity indexes surged and technical sales kicked in.
Some erosion of gains in T-bond futures and stocks helped currency futures turn up from their troughs, brokers said.
Some brokers had noted that currencies showed muted upside reaction Thursday when U.S. T-bonds and stocks fell, which also may have indicated more predilection to a currency drop.
"It's very thin markets, cash and futures," said one floor broker. "There's a lot of action that's not being caught.... It's been a pretty slow, steady grind."
He said one large fund by midday had sold some 2,500 yen as it dropped to the day's low, while another small fund sold about 100 March Swiss francs from $0.7400 to the contract low.
Pressure lifted late as T-bond futures and stocks shaved gains on ideas U.S. rates might rise as early as next month.
Traders said an article in the January 13 issue of Business Week magazine predicting the Fed would hike rates in early 1997 was partly responsible for T-bonds' drop from their peaks.
But they also said some players used the article as an excuse to get out of long positions at week's end, and they said it contained no fresh perspectives on the economic landscape.
They were waiting for traders to return in full force next week to see if Friday's move lower will resume.
Currencies had eased when November U.S. construction spending rose 1.9 pct versus forecasts for down 0.4 percent.
